title: BA1/1922/2018 of MATHURA DUTT JOSHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
BA1 No.1922 of 2018
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.

Mr. Devesh Upreti, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Deputy Advocate General for
the State of Uttarakhand.
 Applicant, who is in judicial custody, in connection
with FIR No.63 of 2018, under Section 8/20 of the
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
Thana Chamwapat, District Champawat has sought his
release on bail.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 Learned counsel for the applicant would argue that
the applicant is a kidney patient. He was shifted to
Lohaghat, District Champawat and when request was made
to this Court, he was sent to Haldwani Hospital but still
there is no Nephrologist and he is being treated by
medicine department. It is argued that one of the kidneys
of the applicant was removed in the year 2018 and another
kidney is 75% damaged. These facts have been stated in
para 9 of the bail application, which are not denied. It is
argued that even today the applicant is in Lohaghat and
there are no advanced medical facilities, therefore, to save
the life of the applicant he may be enlarged on bail.
 In this case, according to the FIR on 28.09.2018
2.10 kg charas was recovered from the possession of the
applicant.
The fact, that the applicant's left kidney was
removed and his right kidney was also damaged, has been
admitted by the State Counsel. At one point time, the
applicant was admitted in Dr. Sushila Tiwari, Government
Hospital, Haldwani. He was shifted to Lohaghat,
Champawat but again in view of his health condition, he
was shifted to Haldwani District Nainital.
 Learned State counsel would admit that there is no
Nephrologist either at Haldwani or at Lohaghat. Patient is
being treated by medicine departments.
 The Court is considering this bail application purely
on the medical ground of the applicant. A person, whose
one kidney is removed another according him is 75%
damaged and it has been admitted by the State that yes the

facts are true that he requires constant monitoring and
follow-up. Applicant is not being treated by any
nephrologists.
 Having considered all the facts and medical reports
and submission of the parties, this Court is of the view that
in order to save the life of the applicant, he may be
enlarged on bail at this stage.
 Accordingly, the bail application is allowed. Let the
applicant Mathura Dutt Joshi be released on bail on
executing personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 29.04.2019
